fonts.family: Noto Sans SC (existing, Chinese badge only; unchanged)

B_neon.placement: Centered under the yellow Chinese-title badge as a brand signature: badge bottom + 64*S gap, then the lockup. The whole stack (English title, badge, logo) is re-centered vertically on its visual cap-top-to-logo-bottom box, sitting 6*S above true center. The kicker line 'No.NN' and the big watermark number are removed; the `no` argument is accepted but not drawn. The lockup is 「朋克英语」: the four characters at 70*S in ZCOOL QingKe HuangYou as hot-pink (255,54,150) neon tubes with a white-hot core and a 3-radius bloom, framed by two cyan (40,236,255) neon corner brackets (top-left 「 and bottom-right 」, 4*S tube width, 30*S arms, 21*S from the glyphs). The glitch is an RGB split: the cyan channel is offset 3*S to the left and a faint red channel 3*S to the right. The logo is screen-blended onto the frame, so it only adds light. Title hl/ghost words, the yellow badge and the background are unchanged from title2.py. Every size is in S units, and the erode kernels are 2u+1 and 4u+1, so they stay odd and proportional; 4K downscaled against 1080p gives a mean pixel diff of 1.4/255. Output is deterministic: identical md5 across reruns.
B_neon.description_zh: 「朋克英语」四个字做成粉红色霓虹灯管的样子，放在黄色中文标题下面，居中，像片头的落款。字是圆头的方块字，灯管中间发白，外面一圈粉色光晕，边缘带一点青色和红色的错位，有故障风的味道。左上角和右下角各有一个青色灯管做的直角引号「」，整个看起来像朋克酒吧墙上挂的招牌。原来的期号和大水印编号都删了，版面重新上下居中，英文大标题还是画面里最显眼的。
B_neon.self_critique: Rounds tried: (1) A tracked 'PUNK ENGLISH' tag line plus a displaced horizontal glitch slice. The tag was wider than the characters and looked detached. The slice made strokes look broken, like a rendering bug, so I dropped both. (2) Added the cyan 「」 corner brackets. They turn plain glowing text into a contained mark that reads as a trademark, and they hint at Chinese quotation marks. I also tried eroding the strokes to make thinner tubes, but that killed the white-hot core and hurt legibility, so I reverted it. (3) Removed a separate magenta 'wall spill' ellipse because it mixed with the green background into a muddy grey haze, and tightened the widest bloom. I also compared tag vs no-tag in place, and bracket-only is cleaner. Strengths: the hierarchy is clear (title > badge > logo). Hot pink against the yellow badge is a real punk palette (yellow + pink), and cyan stays close to the teal-green background. The neon looks believable at 1080p and is crisp at 4K, with the same proportions. Weaknesses: at portrait-phone size (about 0.2x) the characters are only about 13px tall. 朋 is the weakest glyph in this font because its two 月 parts read as stacked boxes, though it is still recognisable. The red half of the RGB split is very faint, so the glitch reads mostly as a cyan fringe. The pink glow adds a fourth hue to the frame, which is lively but less restrained than a single-colour mark. The gap between a descender in the title's last line (e.g. 'Argument') and the badge is tight; that comes from the original 48*S spacing, which I left alone.

fonts.family: Noto Sans SC (variable, wght=900 Black) - used for the 朋克英语 seal characters

A_stamp.placement: Lockup on the title page's bottom row: [yellow Chinese badge] + 30*S gap + [square seal], centred together as one unit (the badge shifts left by about half the seal's width, so the pair sits on the title's centre axis). The seal sits right after the Chinese title, vertically centred on the badge and tilted 7 degrees clockwise. It reads like the name seal a calligrapher presses at the end of a work, which matches "after the title". The seal edge is 1.04 x the badge height (about 154 px at 1080p for 2-line titles, smaller for 3-line titles), so it never rises above the badge row by more than about 8% and keeps clear of the title and the ghost particles. The No.NN kicker and the giant watermark number are gone. The block from the first line's cap-top to the badge bottom is re-centred vertically. The seal is drawn only inside frame_title2, so 朋克英语 appears nowhere else in the video.
A_stamp.description_zh: 在中文标题黄色标签的右边，盖了一枚方形的"朋克英语"印章，玫红色，稍微歪着，像一枚盖在海报上的橡皮章。印章是白文刻法，四个字分成两行（朋克／英语），字形清楚，边缘有自然的磨损和墨点，透出朋克风格。黄色标签和印章作为一组居中摆放；英文大标题仍然最显眼，原来的文章编号和水印数字都已去掉。
A_stamp.self_critique:
Iterations:
(1) ZCOOL QingKe HuangYou in a heavily eroded seal: the edges were blurry and 克 and 语 were unreadable.
(2) Sharper thresholding with fewer voids: legible when large, but the ZCOOL glyphs still broke down at about 50 px per character.
(3) Compared three faces at the real seal size. Noto Serif SC Black lost its thin horizontal strokes, so Noto Sans SC Black won on legibility.
(4) Placement trials. Pressed across the badge edge (a seam seal) made the cut-out characters half yellow and half green, which looked messy. Below the badge felt lonely. The bottom-right corner was disconnected from the title. A centred [badge][seal] lockup was the best of these.
(5) Removed artefacts: round 'rivet' dots on the frame line (from thresholding a thin line, now replaced by a displacement wobble) and round voids (now made from mixed noise scales so they look ragged).

What works now:
- The title is clearly the hero, then the badge, then the seal.
- The hot vermilion-magenta ink is the punk yellow-and-pink poster pairing next to the badge, and it pops against the dark green as a complementary colour.
- 朋克英语 is still readable at 480 px frame width.
- The texture is seeded, so the mark looks identical in every video, which is right for a brand mark.
- S=2 output matches S=1: seal bounding box (1270,731)-(1439,900) at S=1 vs (1272,730.5)-(1441.5,900.5) after halving the 4K box. Two identical runs give byte-identical PNGs.

Honest weaknesses:
- The seal uses the same Noto Sans family as the badge. That is less distinctive than custom lettering; the brand identity comes from the seal form, tilt, frame and wear rather than the letterforms.
- At 1080p each character is only about 50 px, fine on a phone but it is a small mark.
- The badge is no longer on the exact title axis; it sits about 100 px left because the lockup is centred as a pair.
- The 2x2 seal reads row by row (朋克 / 英语), not in the traditional right-to-left column order. I chose this on purpose so modern viewers read it correctly.
- I downloaded and tested ZCOOL QingKe HuangYou, Ma Shan Zheng and Noto Serif SC (three fonts, over the one-or-two limit), rejected them all and deleted them. The final design uses no downloaded font.
- I did not touch the inherited ghost-particle code, which uses 260*S particles, so the 4K ghost word looks a bit denser than the 1080p one.
- Exploration renders are in the work/ subfolder.

C_graffiti.placement: The kicker and the watermark number are gone. The stack is re-centred on the visible ink: title (1-3 lines), then a 48px gap, then the yellow Chinese badge, then a 56px gap, then the graffiti tag. The tag is horizontally centred on its lettering, not on its splatter. It works as a signature lockup below the badge, as if sprayed onto the poster under the title. The 56px gap is a little larger than the 48px gap between title and badge, so title and badge read as one unit and the tag reads as a sign-off. The tag is about 96px per glyph at S=1, around 460px wide counting splatter, against a title cap height of about 120px, so the title stays the hero. A corner placement (PLACEMENT='corner') is still in the code but is not used: the tag looked like a sticker stuck in the corner and was cut off at the bottom edge.
C_graffiti.description_zh: 片头去掉了期号和大水印数字，标题、黄色中文条和品牌标志整体垂直居中。黄色中文标题条下方居中放着一个涂鸦喷漆风格的「朋克英语」标志：毛笔字体，亮粉色渐变填充，外面一圈细黄描边（跟中文条的黄色一样），再加深色外框和投影。整体微微向右上倾斜，带几道往下流的油漆滴痕、喷溅的小点和一个小闪光，下面一行很小的“PUNK ENGLISH”。粉配黄是经典的朋克配色，在深绿背景上很跳，但个头比英文标题小得多，不会喧宾夺主。
C_graffiti.self_critique: Iterations. (1) The earlier pass in this directory compared four fonts (Zhi Mang Xing, Liu Jian Mao Cao, Ma Shan Zheng, ZCOOL KuaiLe; comparison image in work/fontcmp.png). Liu Jian Mao Cao is unreadable as 朋克英语 at phone size and Zhi Mang Xing's 朋 is odd, so I chose Ma Shan Zheng: the most legible brush font that still looks hand-made. I built the tag from it: per-character jitter in rotation, offset and scale, a dark outline, a block shadow, a gravity-correct paint drip under 朋, 克 and 语, splatter and mist, a 4-point glint, a 4-degree upward tilt, and a tiny tracked 'PUNK ENGLISH' line. (2) That version used 92px with a dark outline only. The outline was close in value to the dark-green background, so the tag read as pink text with a shadow rather than a finished piece. I tested no keyline, a yellow keyline at 2.2% and 3.2% of the em, and a white keyline (work/cmp_keyline.png). The 2.2% yellow keyline won: it reads like a real graffiti piece (fill, keyline, outline, 3D shadow), and it reuses the badge yellow (255,214,64), so the pink is tied into the palette. Pink plus yellow is also the classic punk pairing. The 3.2% keyline was too heavy and white looked weaker. (3) I enlarged the tag from 92 to 96px for phone legibility; 104px started to crowd the vertical space on 3-line titles. I also widened the badge-to-logo gap from 40 to 56px so title and badge group together. Checks: at 640x360 (phone preview) 朋克英语 is clearly readable. Top and bottom margins are balanced in all three tests: about 90/90 for t03, the 3-line case. Nothing overlaps or is cut off. The output is byte-identical across two runs. The S=2 render downscaled to 1080p puts the pink ink box within 1px of the S=1 version. The fontTools cmap has all four glyphs (uni670B, uni514B, uni82F1, uni8BED), and each renders differently from .notdef. All MaxFilter sizes go through odd(). I deleted the three unused trial fonts, so only one downloaded font remains. Remaining weaknesses: pink is a third accent colour next to the yellow-orange highlight words, so a conservative reviewer may find the page busier than the stamp or wordmark directions. The 'PUNK ENGLISH' line is about 13px at S=1, so it is decorative only and unreadable on a phone. The splatter burst on the right makes the whole lockup look about 15px right-heavy even though the lettering is centred. The S=2 render takes about 60s because the tag is supersampled 3x and the drip search uses Python loops; this is acceptable for a single still frame. The function no longer reads any env knobs other than VIDEO_S, through render.py.

fonts.family: Inter (existing, wght 800 for the PUNK ENGLISH sub-line)

D_wordmark.placement: The lockup sits centred below the yellow Chinese title badge, 64*S below it. The stack runs from the cap top of title line 1 to the bottom of the lockup and is centred vertically as one block (nudged up 6*S for optical balance). The kicker and the watermark number are removed; the 'no' argument is accepted but not displayed. The lockup is a horizontal app-style mark. On the left is a rounded square (radius 0.26) with a diagonal yellow(255,214,64)->orange(255,120,80) gradient, the same colours as the highlighted title words. It carries a chunky flat-top lightning bolt in dark ink (14,36,29), is tilted -6 degrees for some punk attitude, and has a faint orange halo (35%). On the right, 朋克英语 is set in ZCOOL QingKe HuangYou at 60*S in off-white (248,250,246), with a light faux-bold stroke (0.018 em) so it holds its own next to the Inter 900 title. Under it, a teal (94,234,212) PUNK ENGLISH in Inter 800 at 15*S is justified to exactly the wordmark width. At 1080p the lockup is about 292x78 px, roughly a quarter of the badge width, so the title and badge stay dominant. Drop-in signature: frame_title2(no,en,zh,hl,ghost,out,variant=1). Everything scales with S, the lockup is supersampled 4x for smooth polygon edges, and the ghost particles use a seeded random.Random(3). check_brand_glyphs() checks the font cmap and also compares each character against the .notdef render.
D_wordmark.description_zh: 标题下方、黄色中文标题条的正下方，放了一个像App图标一样的品牌标志：左边是一个微微倾斜的黄橙渐变圆角方块，里面有一道深色闪电；右边是粗壮方正的白色「朋克英语」四个字，下面配一行小小的青绿色“PUNK ENGLISH”。整体干净、有力，颜色和标题的黄橙高亮、青绿色调呼应，英文标题依然是画面主角，编号已全部去掉。
D_wordmark.self_critique:
I rendered and looked at each version. v1 used Feather's thin bolt and the unbolded wordmark, and the logo looked too light next to the Inter 900 title. v2 added a chunky custom bolt and a 0.025 em faux-bold; 朋 started to fill in. v3 brought the stroke down to 0.018 em, raised the size to 60, added the -6 degree icon tilt and a subtle orange halo, made the sub-line Inter 800, and widened the badge-to-logo gap to 64.

Strengths: it reads as a real brand mark (an app-icon-plus-wordmark lockup like a modern edtech brand), and the colours come straight from the existing palette. Hierarchy is clear (title > badge > logo). 朋克英语 is still readable in a 480 px-wide phone mockup (the PUNK ENGLISH sub-line is illegible at that size). The 4K render matches the 1080p one: the logo box is exactly 2x (814,876,1106,954 -> 1628,1752,2213,1909). Output is deterministic (byte-identical when re-rendered), and title2.py was not modified.

Weaknesses: on a phone, PUNK ENGLISH becomes texture, and its wide justified tracking (about 0.4 em) may look slightly loose to some eyes. The faux-bold stroke makes the rounded ZCOOL corners a little softer than a true heavy cut would. On 3-line titles at the maximum size (t03) the stack is tall, leaving margins of about 115 px top and 125 px bottom: fine, but tighter than t02. The tilt and halo make the mark playful rather than strictly corporate. If judges want a calmer mark, brand_lockup(tilt=0, glow=0) is a one-line change.

fonts.family: Ma Shan Zheng (brush, used for 英)
Noto Sans SC 900 (existing, used for 朋 and 语)

E_ransom.placement: Centered directly below the yellow Chinese-title badge, as the last item in the vertical stack (title, then badge, then logo). It sits 46*S below the badge, so it reads as a brand sign-off that comes after the title. The kicker and the watermark number are removed. The whole stack is centered optically: the empty space above the first line's cap height is subtracted, so the top and bottom margins come out about equal (about 115px and 120px on t01). The logo is about 370x150px at 1080p (LOGO_SCALE=1.2), clearly smaller and quieter than the badge and title. frame_title2(no,en,zh,hl,ghost,out,variant=1) keeps the original signature (no is ignored). It also returns the logo's bounding box (x,y,w,h), which only the preview and crop helpers use.
E_ransom.description_zh: “朋克英语”四个字像70年代朋克海报上的勒索信拼贴：每个字剪在一块不同颜色的纸片上，有黑底白字、荧光粉、米白纸和亮黄色，纸片微微倾斜，边缘有撕纸毛边，角上贴着米色纸胶带。下面有一条很小的黑色打标签机胶条，印着“PUNK ENGLISH”。整个标志紧凑地放在黄色中文标题条正下方，英文大标题仍然是画面主角。
E_ransom.self_critique:
Iterations:
(1) In the first render 克 and 语 were cut off. The glyphs were centered on the average of the polygon points, and the extra points on torn edges pulled that average off. Fixed by centering on the paper rectangle.
(2) The four tiles looked too uniform, like a row of squares. Fixed by giving each piece its own size and aspect (克 tall, 英 wide), more vertical jitter, separate tilts for paper and glyph, and different overlap per pair. The 朋 piece got an uneven magazine margin, and the tape was made more opaque because the translucent tape looked muddy on the green.
(3) Added a tiny Dymo label reading PUNK ENGLISH. It ties the cluster together into a lockup. It covered the bottom of 英, so I moved it down and shrank that glyph.
(4) Scaled the logo up 1.2x for phone legibility. The glyphs are now about 55 to 65px at 1080p, and 朋克英语 still reads clearly when the frame is shown at half size. Then I made the halftone and grain subtler, because the pink looked like towel fabric.

Checks that passed:
- All four characters have glyphs in every font used (fontTools cmap).
- Output is deterministic: identical md5 on re-render.
- The S=2 render downscaled to 1080p matches S=1 (mean pixel difference about 2 levels).
- The 4K logo is crisp, because the pieces are drawn at 4x supersampling and resized premultiplied, so there are no dark fringes.

Weaknesses:
- Hot pink is a new accent color outside the green/yellow palette. It is intentional for the punk feel, but it is the loudest spot on the frame after the title glow.
- The brush-style 英 has thin strokes and reads a little lighter than the other three characters at very small sizes.
- The PUNK ENGLISH label is only texture at phone size.
- Rendering at S=2 takes about 15s per frame, mostly from the original title effects.

Extra files: logo_crop_4k.png, plus the preview.py and crops.py dev helpers. The renderer must run with cwd=video and video on PYTHONPATH, exactly like title2.py.
